_schemaNote: toneCurve points are [x, y] pairs, e.g. [0.25, 0.24] -- NOT {"x":...,"y":...} objects. This matches CGPoint's actual Codable wire format (an unkeyed 2-element array), confirmed against CoreGraphics.swiftinterface -- {x,y} was a real bug shipped once (decode failure on device, every variant). Digicam/Travel Film authors: copy this format.
_tuningNote: TUNED from a hand-graded reference image (Lightroom units), converted onto CoreImage's parameter ranges. See EditOp.swift/EditEngine.swift and the session's own report for the exact conversion math (EV->brightness via a mid-gray anchor, LR contrast/saturation percent points -> CIColorControls multiplier offset from 1.0, temperature given as a mired-space warming delta applied against a fixed 6500K/tint-0 baseline (matches EditEngine.temperatureTint's own fixed source neutral), tint sign-flipped after empirically verifying this filter's magenta/green direction on-device rather than assuming Lightroom's convention carries over, 0-255 tone-curve values normalized to 0-1, bloom radius-as-percent-of-width converted to pixels against the 1280px preview reference width). Two of the three variants' tone curves were reduced from the reference's 7 points to CIToneCurve's required 5 by dropping the two innermost 1/8-and-7/8 handles (keeping 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1) -- the dropped points were within ~2/255 of the straight line between their surviving neighbors, so the spline through the remaining 5 approximates them closely. The reference's separate 'faded blacks' value was NOT applied via the fade op -- it's numerically identical to each variant's own tone-curve black point (point0), i.e. the same data named twice, and applying both would double the shadow lift. fade is dropped from this pack's chain entirely; vibrance is new (CIVibrance has no colorControls equivalent -- see EditOp.swift).
